faq.q: What kind of homes are over $1.8M in Langley?
faq.a: Typical listings in this range: acreage estates, including equestrian properties with barns and arenas in Campbell Valley, large new-build estates in Salmon River, a 39.5-acre multi-building estate in Otter District, and Brookswood properties with coach houses and redevelopment potential. Executive homes in Willoughby and heritage homes in Fort Langley also come up at this price.

faq.q: Can an over-$1.8M Langley acreage add another home?
faq.a: It depends on the property's ALR status and zoning, not the price. On ALR land, the Agricultural Land Commission allows one main house up to 500 m² plus at most one additional home of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha), with a suite only inside the main house. The Township's small-scale multi-unit rules don't help on big lots: they apply only to serviced lots of 4,050 m² or less inside the Urban Containment Boundary.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house to a house in Langley?
faq.a: BC's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow more homes on many urban lots, but each municipality sets the details and many lots are excluded. Check the lot's zoning with the municipality before you plan a suite or coach house.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in Langley?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.
